evidence.reason: scanPatch extracts `+++`/`---` candidates but strips `a/` or `b/` only when unquoted. With Git's default path quoting, a candidate can be `"b/secr\303\251t.env"`; the loaded path rule `\.env$` then does not match because of the retained quote/escapes. The comment states the project-rule scan covers removed lines (`secret_scan_diff`), so this is an implementation bug in existing secret-scan behavior, not a new hardening requirement. When gitleaks is unavailable, removed secret content in a quoted-path deletion can bypass a path-scoped project rule. Decode Git-quoted paths or refuse undecodable candidates before matching rules.
